catalogue_provenance.status: P9 pass landed. Enforced per field by scripts/build-registry.mjs and asserted by scripts/check-registry.mjs, not held as a principle.
catalogue_provenance.rule: Every product field carries its own provenance entry naming the record it came from, or it is blank and says what is owed. Four bases: confirmed (read off the organisation's own page), sourced (read off a named third party), derived (transformed from a named source, with the transformation stated), none (blank).

per_field.summary: 0/16 populated — none 16. Every one blanked: no description was ever read verbatim, and the previous text was written from general knowledge.
per_field.eligibility: 3/16 populated — derived 3, none 13. `stated` is read from the source; the enum arrays are a mapping into this schema's vocabulary and may never claim basis `sourced` — the build rejects it.
per_field.requirements: 3/16 populated — none 13, sourced 3. This is what effort derives from.
per_field.kind: 16/16 populated — derived 16. Classification into this schema's vocabulary, so never `sourced`.

catalogue_provenance.effort: DERIVED, never stored. A stored grading is an opinion and it is the denominator of the ranking — the defect the Q4 audit found. It is now computed at read time from the record's sourced requirements via data/vantage.config.json effort_from_requirements. A record whose requirements were never read has no effort; the ranking uses the configured unknown cost and the card says so. The build rejects any record that stores an `effort` field.
catalogue_provenance.effort_decision: Sourced, not moved. The Q4 held_opposition was right that moving effort into data/vantage.config.json would relocate an unsourced claim into the file this project's own Q3 answer named as the dangerous straddle. What moved there is the DERIVATION RULE, which is an editorial weight and belongs in config; the inputs it reads are sourced facts on the record.
catalogue_provenance.also_fixed: effort_tolerance was removed from fit.criteria. It was double-counted — effort is already the denominator of return-on-effort, so weighting it in the numerator moved the same fact twice — and it pointed at call.effort, which no longer exists.
catalogue_provenance.guards_tested: Three violations were planted and rejected: a summary written with no source, an eligibility claiming basis `sourced` rather than `derived`, and an effort stored back on a record.
catalogue_provenance.blocking: A listing generated today would carry: name, org, url, a deadline for 6/16, eligibility and requirements for 3/16, an award figure for 1/16. Every other field is blank by contract rather than plausible. That is shippable in shape but thin in coverage; the remaining work is sourcing, not schema.
catalogue_provenance.owed: Eligibility and requirements for 13 records; deadlines for 10; award figures for 15; primary confirmation for all 6 sourced deadlines, none of which is `confirmed` because the build container cannot reach most organisation pages directly.

policy.detail: No two coworkers in a non-terminal state may claim overlapping path globs in the same repository. Overlap is a merge conflict that has not happened yet.

policy.rule: A live base branch must be declared as inherited, not assumed.
policy.detail: If a project's base_branch is a branch another live project is still pushing to, the dependency is real and must be visible here. Undeclared, it reads as an independent branch and diverges silently.

policy.rule: A blocked coworker is an operator debt.
policy.detail: Blocked means something is owed by a person or a sibling session. Every blocked coworker carries either an unblocked_by naming the action taken, or an open plan entry.

policy.rule: Terminal work is retired, not left running.
policy.detail: A coworker whose project is done or whose session failed is archived. An idle session nobody has read in over fourteen days is surfaced for a decision rather than left to expire quietly.

policy.rule: A ritual without a Routine is an intention.
policy.detail: Every project marked ritual: true must have a Routine bound to it. Recurring work that depends on somebody remembering is not recurring work.

policy.rule: Deployment goes to a declared environment.
policy.detail: A coworker spawned for a project in this repository lands in the environment named here. Sessions outside it are legacy and are marked so, never silently adopted.

policy.rule: An inherited base is merged, not assumed.
policy.detail: A session's source revision is fixed at creation. If a project declares inherits but its source_revision is not the upstream branch, the inheritance exists only on paper until the upstream branch is merged into the working branch.

policy.rule: A shared file is owned by one project; the rest declare the claim.
policy.detail: public/index.html, package.json and README.md are touched by every subtree. The shell owns them. A project that must change one declares it in claims_disputed so the collision is visible before the second merge, not after.

policy.rule: No product claim without a record behind it.
policy.detail: Engineering and product are different registers with different truth conditions. An engineering claim is true if it works; a product claim is true if a record backs it. Any catalogue field — a listing, a description, a spec sheet, a Shopify product body — extracts from a named record: a tech spec, a patent filing, a production note, a measurement. Where no record exists the field stays blank and is marked. Generated copy is not extracted copy, and a blank field is a finding while a fabricated one is a defect.
policy.applies_to: any project whose vantages_held include content-marketing, or that declares produces_artifact

policy.rule: A subtree registers itself in its own pull request.
policy.detail: The shell owns public/index.html, but the card announcing a subtree belongs to the subtree's PR, not the shell's. If the shell carries the card, the shell merging alone ships a dead link on the front page. Enforced structurally in scripts/check-tiers.mjs: every .card--link href must resolve to an index.html present on the branch.
policy.established: 2026-08-29. The simulator session re-added its own card to the shell's file to close a gap this file had raised against it — the right instinct, filed one branch too early. Taking it onto the shell branch produced a front page linking /simulator/, which does not exist there.

policy.rule: A stacked pull request targets the branch it stacks on.
policy.detail: A project that declares inherits must open its PR against the inherited project's branch, not against the branch that branch came from. Otherwise the PR's diff shows the upstream's work as its own, a reviewer cannot see what the project actually changed, and merging it lands the upstream through the wrong door — which silently overrides whatever merge order was arbitrated.
policy.established: 2026-08-29. PR #3 targets the placeholder base while its branch already carries the shell, so its diff is 55 files of which 20+ are the shell's. PR #2, targeting the venue branch, shows only its own work. The difference is one field on the pull request.

mechanisms.name: Delivering a message to a sibling cloud session
steps: create_trigger with persistent_session_id and no schedule
delete_trigger once delivered; log the operation here instead
constraints: ListAgents does not reach cloud siblings; there is no direct peer channel.
update_trigger cannot edit the prompt of a routine that fires into another session — a correction is a new trigger, not an edit.
The target cannot reply. Read its state with get_session instead of expecting an answer.

fire_trigger with a `text` argument does not deliver into the bound session. Established by controlled comparison on 2026-08-29: three fires without `text` returned session_id = cse_ + the target's own suffix and the target acted; two fires with `text` returned unrelated cse_ ids and neither target was touched — one had not been updated since six minutes BEFORE the fire. Put everything in the prompt and fire bare. The returned session_id is the delivery receipt: if its suffix does not match the target, nothing arrived.
mechanisms.note: Established by use on 2026-08-29; each constraint was hit, not read.
mechanisms.verification: Do not treat a fire as delivered because the call returned 200. Check the returned session_id suffix, and check the target's updated_at moved. A relay that silently no-ops looks exactly like a coworker choosing not to answer.

vantages.note: A role is a vantage, not a person. One coworker holds several. A vantage with no holder is a gap and is recorded as one, because the questions that vantage would have asked do not get asked by anybody else. Full definitions and the arbitration rules live in fleet/questions.json.
vantages.engineering: What the thing is and whether it works. Tech specs, retrofit, tolerances.
vantages.creative-director: What it looks like it is. Coherence of the image across every surface.
vantages.producer: Duration, contingency, cost of being wrong. Survival of contact with a date and a room.
vantages.content-marketing: What is claimed in public and on what record. Catalogue copy, listing, description.
